 Thousands hit the streets for 51st running of Marine Corps Marathon
 By WTOP Staff 
 October 25, 2026 | 
 7:29 AM 
 | 
 The 51st Marine Corps Marathon is underway as thousands of runners hit the streets Sunday, traveling from Arlington, through parts of D.C. and back into Virginia to complete the 26.2 miles affectionately known as “the People’s Marathon.”
 The runners set off at around 7:20 a.m. in chilly temperatures, likely in the 40s, but the weather will warm up as the race progresses.
 While the route and many of the traditions remain the same this year, the organizers have introduced some new elements.
 As usual, the race is bringing a long list of road closures to the area. View them at this link .
 Related stories
 The Marine Corps Marathon returns this weekend. What’s new this year? 
 A champion reveals her tips on last minute prep for Marine Corps Marathon

 In years past, runners got to choose where they ran in the pack and stood near signs next to their projected run times. This time, runners instead gather in corrals based on their anticipated finish times.
 Corral numbers are located on racers’ bibs. Marines will organize the runners as they get to the starting line near the Pentagon.
 Much like last year, the finish line at the grounds of the Marine Corps War Memorial is closed to spectators. Instead, family and friends can reconnect with their runners at the finish festival in Rosslyn.
 Reporting from the Marine Corps Marathon, WTOP’s Luke Lukert contributed to this report.

 Frosty start ahead of Marine Corps Marathon gives way to sunny Sunday across DC area
 By Will Vitka 
 October 25, 2026 | 
 4:50 AM 
 | 
 More pleasant fall weather is expected Sunday in the D.C. region, as thousands of runners take to the streets for the Marine Corps Marathon.
For runners participating in “the People’s Marathon,” the forecast calls for a cold start, but favorable conditions as the race gets underway.
Patchy frost is possible early Sunday, particularly west of Interstate 95.
Temperatures are expected to hover around 40 degrees when the main race begins at 7:20 a.m., before climbing into the 50s by midmorning. Light winds and plenty of sunshine are expected throughout the morning, with afternoon highs around 65 degrees.
